_comment: WHERE EVERY DECLARED-SECRET NAME'S VALUE ACTUALLY COMES FROM. Read and checked
by .ci/scripts/quality/check_secret_supply.py; read that module's docstring before
editing, because every rule below is enforced there and none of it is advisory.
NO VALUE OF ANY KIND IS RECORDED HERE. Names, kinds, destinations and one project
UUID that .ci/config/bws-secret-map.json already carries in the clear. .ci/lib/
bws-env.sh:16-18 states the same rule for the fetch helper and is the reason it
holds for this file too: this repository is public and a gate's output is a log
surface.
TWO HALVES, AND THEY ARE DELIBERATELY IN ONE FILE.
`residue` is DERIVED and then classified: the names env-manifest.json puts in the
`secret` shard that .ci/config/bws-secret-map.json does not hold. `secret` means
'supplied by the vault or by a GitHub secret', so a name in that shard which no
vault holds is a name whose supply is UNSTATED. Every one gets a kind and a
reason here. The gate asserts set equality with the derived residue in BOTH
directions, so this half can neither be trimmed to escape a finding nor
pre-loaded with one.
`dotenv` is the TRUNCATION SPEC for private/account/.env -- one destination per
assigned name, set-equal with the file while it exists. The terminal state is NO
FILE AT ALL (agent/plans/PLAN-account-env-to-bws.md T18): the bootstrap token
lives in ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/rediacc/bws-access-token, and every
other destination is a place the value comes from instead.
`consumers` is the THIRD half: the named profiles `python3 -m
rediacc_ci.core.bws_env exec --profile P -- CMD` binds into a child process
(account-dev, account-e2e, deploy-bench, rotation, backup-plane, publish-media).
Each spec uses the `NAME > LOCAL` grammar; the gate asserts every NAME resolves
in the vault map and that no spec is a wildcard.
THE HALVES CHECK EACH OTHER, WHICH IS WHY THEY SHARE A FILE. A `ci-shared`
destination is FALSE unless the vault map holds the name, a `ci-shared-alias`
destination is FALSE unless the map holds the name its `aliases` row names, and a
`dev.defaults.env` destination is FALSE if the map holds the name. A name headed for
the COMMITTED defaults file that is classified `secret` is a credential about to be
committed, and the gate refuses it by name.
ONE PROJECT, AND THE OPERATOR RULED IT STAYS ONE (2026-09-24, PLAN-account-env-to-bws
Q1, Q2, Q4). The dev keypair is seeded as `_DEV` names, the admin credentials sit
beside everything else, and the dev SES key is an alias of the EU entry. No
`dev-shared` or `admin-bootstrap` project exists or is planned.
AND THE GATE STARTS ENFORCING THE SEEDED STATE THE MOMENT THE PROJECT EXISTS. A
seeded name lands in bws-secret-map.json on the next refresh, leaves the derived
residue, and its entry here reds as RESOLVED with instructions to drain it. No
edit to the gate is needed for that to happen.
HOW TO ADD OR REMOVE AN ENTRY. Do neither by hand-writing a set. The gate names
the exact name and the exact half, and there is deliberately no bulk reseed verb:
a blanket rewrite is how a fresh violation gets absorbed alongside a legitimate
drain, and 75 entries is small enough to edit one line at a time.

kinds.runner-minted: Minted per job by GitHub Actions or by an action, and never stored anywhere. A vault entry for one of these would be a second, longer-lived credential for something the runner already hands out with a one-hour life.
kinds.sdk-alias: Not a credential of its own: the spelling an SDK insists on, exported at the call site from a name a vault DOES hold. `alias_of` names that entry and the gate checks it resolves in .ci/config/bws-secret-map.json, so an alias cannot point at nothing.
kinds.generated: Produced at run time by the process that consumes it: a key pair written into a temp dir, a token seeded into a preview database, a password composed for a throwaway container. There is no value to store, only a recipe.
kinds.user-supplied: Typed by the END USER of the shipped product on their own machine. It is in the secret shard because it carries a secret value; it is not in any vault because it is not our value.
kinds.fixture-default: Has a non-secret default committed in the tree, so an unset environment still runs. Storing it would give a fixture a credential.
kinds.github-secret-only: Lives as a GitHub Actions secret and was deliberately not mirrored into the vault. The BLOCKER for each is in `why`.
kinds.not-a-credential: In the secret shard but not a secret: a name fragment, a suffix, a switch. Recorded here rather than quietly reshuffled between shards, because moving it is `check:ci-env-manifest`'s call and not this gate's.
kinds.bootstrap-irreducible: The credential that fetches the others. It cannot come from the store it unlocks. Exactly one name may carry this kind and the gate enforces that.
kinds.dev-shared: A real development credential with no dev store to come from. The project `dev-shared` does not exist -- the live vault holds ONE project, `ci-shared` -- and only the web vault can create it, so this is door:operator-only. Every entry with this kind is PRINTED BY NAME on every run.

ACCOUNT_BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID.why: The Worker binding name, never a vault entry since the shared pair was revoked on 2026-10-15 (agent/plans/PLAN-backup-credential-isolation.md B7). Each environment's own vault pair is bound under this name: cd-deploy-account.yml and set_account_worker_secrets.py pick _STABLE or _EDGE by target, and the backup-push-{stable,edge,bench} and deploy-bench profiles alias _STABLE, _EDGE or _BENCH. alias_of names the stable pair; check:ci-backup-credential-isolation pins that each consumer takes exactly one environment's pair.

ACCOUNT_BACKUP_S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.why: The Worker binding name, never a vault entry since the shared pair was revoked on 2026-10-15 (agent/plans/PLAN-backup-credential-isolation.md B7). Each environment's own vault pair is bound under this name, as for ACCOUNT_BACKUP_S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID.

ACCOUNT_CONFIG_SERVER_KEY.why: The Worker binding name, never a vault entry: each region and channel has its own key, ACCOUNT_CONFIG_SERVER_KEY_<SUFFIX>_<STABLE|EDGE> or _BENCH (agent/plans/PLAN-config-server-key.md K2), and set_account_worker_secrets or deploy_bench pushes the one its target names under this binding.

AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID.why: the AWS SDK reads only this spelling; the deploy scripts export it from the R2 key immediately before calling the SDK.

AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.why: the secret half of the pair above, exported at the same two lines.

AWS_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID.why: The Worker binding name, fed from the regional vault entry AWS_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID_EU in CI. On a developer machine `bws_env exec --profile account-dev` binds the same entry under this name (`AWS_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID_EU > AWS_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID`), on the operator's ruling to keep aliasing the EU key rather than mint a dev IAM user (agent/plans/PLAN-account-env-to-bws.md Q4).

AWS_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY.why: The Worker binding name, fed from the regional vault entry AWS_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY_EU in CI. On a developer machine `bws_env exec --profile account-dev` binds the same entry under this name (`AWS_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY_EU > AWS_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`), on the operator's ruling to keep aliasing the EU key rather than mint a dev IAM user (agent/plans/PLAN-account-env-to-bws.md Q4).

BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN.why: the fetcher refuses without it and says why in as many words: no bws verb mints or rotates a machine-account token, so the credential that opens the store cannot be kept in the store. It lives in its own token file (`bws_env.token_path()`, ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/rediacc/bws-access-token, mode 0600), never in private/account/.env (agent/plans/PLAN-account-env-to-bws.md T1).

CHECKS_TOKEN.why: rediacc_ci.ci.detect_pointer_bump documents it as `plain GITHUB_TOKEN; checks:read on console` and ci.yml supplies github.token. The runner mints it.

DOCKERHUB_PASSWORD.why: BLOCKER: an anonymous Docker Hub pull works and the gate says so at its own :29 -- the credential only raises the rate limit. Mirroring it into the vault would put a third-party account password in a store every CI job can read, to buy a quota.

E2E_ACCOUNT_API_TOKEN.why: rediacc_ci.testrun.start_account CREATES the subscribed user and echoes the resulting bearer token into GITHUB_ENV. It exists for one suite run against one throwaway account server.

E2E_SSH_KEY.why: a path to a key file, defaulted with `??` in every reading test. The key is the one the e2e machine was provisioned with, not a stored secret.

GH_APP_TOKEN.why: the app-token action's output again, under a second spelling, used to rewrite a git URL for the submodule fetch.

GH_TOKEN.why: the gh CLI's own variable. Every site sets it inline from a token minted moments earlier; nothing reads a stored value.

GITHUB_PAT.why: documented in that module's ENVIRONMENT paragraph as `app token; contents:read on the submodule repos`. The name says PAT and the value is an App token, which is worth knowing and is not worth a vault entry.

GITHUB_TOKEN.why: the runner's own per-job token. It is in the secret shard because it carries a credential; it can never be in a vault.

MATRIX_SECRET_SUFFIX.why: a region suffix, `EU` or `US` or `ASIA`, used to BUILD the name of a secret. resolve_account_deploy_config.py requires it through _require and does not re-emit it. It is arguably misfiled in the secret shard; that is check:ci-env-manifest's call, so it is recorded here instead of moved.

PGPASSWORD.why: the Rediaccfile composes it for a tutorial's throwaway Postgres container and hands the same value to the app. Nothing outside that one deployment ever sees it.

REDIACC_STORE_MASTER_PASSWORD.why: documented to users as the config store's master password, which opens its password slot for headless remote-config unlock. It is the user's password for the user's config, and this repository must never hold one.

REDIACC_MASTER_PASSWORD.why: read at config-file-storage.ts before falling back to the interactive resolver. Same argument: it is the user's value.

REDIACC_TOKEN.why: the account api-token for whoever is running the CLI. CI paths get theirs from E2E_ACCOUNT_API_TOKEN or SMOKE_TEST_TOKEN, both generated.

RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY.why: the compose file defaults it to `rustfsadmin` in four places. It is the login of a local S3 stand-in that listens on a loopback port.

RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY.why: the secret half of the pair above, with the same committed default.

SMOKE_TEST_TOKEN.why: rediacc_ci.testrun.seed_smoke SEEDS the token into the preview D1 and echoes it to GITHUB_OUTPUT. It is created and consumed inside one run.

SSH_KEY.why: a PATH to a key file under $RUNNER_TEMP, which check:ci-workflows quotes as its own plant fixture. The key is generated by the staging provision step.

TOKEN.why: check_bws_map.py's GH_CLI_ENV names it beside APP_TOKEN and REPO as a gh-CLI passthrough. A bare `TOKEN` is never a stored name.

TUTORIAL_SSH_KEY.why: defaulted at tutorial-helpers.sh to $HOME/.renet/staging/.ssh/id_rsa. A path to a key the VM lab made, not a value.

NFPM_APK_KEY_FILE.why: build_linux_pkg.py sets this itself at run time from the GPG material already unsealed for the release (see the os.environ[...] assignments around line 539). It is never stored: the value exists only inside the signing process that consumes it, so a vault entry would be a second, longer-lived copy of a credential that currently lives for the length of one build.

APK_RSA_PRIVATE_KEY.why: BLOCKER: NOTHING SUPPLIES THIS TODAY, and the kind is the closest of the nine rather than a claim that a GitHub secret currently holds it -- read this `why`, not the kind. apk is declared-unsigned: check-release-signing-coverage.sh carries the exemption and records it as VERIFIED 2026-09-06 by building both ways, and build_linux_pkg.py says in its own words that APK_RSA_PRIVATE_KEY is set by nothing here and is absent from bws-secret-map.json, so nfpm.yaml's apk signature block reads an env var never populated. It stays in the `secret` shard because the name carries key material the day anyone mints one. Mint an RSA key, put it in the vault, and both this entry and that exemption go.

REDIACC_LOGIN_EMAIL.why: read by packages/cli/src/services/account/subscription-password-auth.ts for the headless account sign-in (`rdc subscription login --password-stdin`, `rdc config remote master-password change`). It is the user's own account credential; the one repository caller, rediacc_ci.ops.login_bench, fills it in a child environment from the bench-login profile's REDIACC_BENCH_* values, never from a vault entry of this name.

REDIACC_LOGIN_PASSWORD.why: read by packages/cli/src/services/account/subscription-password-auth.ts for the headless account sign-in (`rdc subscription login --password-stdin`, `rdc config remote master-password change`). It is the user's own account credential; the one repository caller, rediacc_ci.ops.login_bench, fills it in a child environment from the bench-login profile's REDIACC_BENCH_* values, never from a vault entry of this name.

REDIACC_LOGIN_TOTP.why: read by packages/cli/src/services/account/subscription-password-auth.ts for the headless account sign-in (`rdc subscription login --password-stdin`, `rdc config remote master-password change`). It is the user's own account credential; the one repository caller, rediacc_ci.ops.login_bench, fills it in a child environment from the bench-login profile's REDIACC_BENCH_* values, never from a vault entry of this name.

destinations.token-file: The bootstrap token's own file, ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/rediacc/bws-access-token (mode 0600), which `bws_env.read_token()` reads when the variable is unset. Only a `bootstrap_names` credential may route here.
destinations.ci-shared: Already in the vault under the same name. The local assignment is a DUPLICATE, deleted once `compare` reports MATCH and its readers bind it through a `consumers` profile. The gate checks the name really is in .ci/config/bws-secret-map.json.
destinations.ci-shared-alias: In the vault under ANOTHER name, which `aliases` records (`STORE > LOCAL` in a profile). The gate checks every such row has an alias and that the alias target is in .ci/config/bws-secret-map.json.
destinations.dev.defaults.env: Not a secret. Moves to the COMMITTED private/account/dev.defaults.env, which then IS the documentation. The gate refuses any name here that the env manifest classifies `secret`, because that is a credential one commit away from being public.
destinations.derived: Computed at run time from GATEWAY_PORT by the process that needs it (account_dev passes WEBAUTHN_ORIGIN to the gateway; rdc.sh --dev reads the port from .account-state). Nothing stores it.
destinations.dead: Empty in the file, and every reader treats empty as unset (private/account/src/entry/on-premise.ts), so deleting the line changes nothing.

account-dev.why: `./run.sh account dev` (rediacc_ci.core.account) re-execs itself under this profile. The six DEV signing and session keys are required; everything else only switches on an optional feature, so a store without it still starts the gateway. CI's drills leg mints throwaway keys into the job environment instead, and the shell wins.

account-e2e.why: `./run.sh account test e2e` (account_test_e2e). The suite drives a running gateway; the one value it takes from the store is the root address the admin tests log in as.

backup-plane.why: rediacc_ci.drills.backup_local_plane starts a dev gateway against a local RustFS. It needs the DEV keys and nothing else: ACCOUNT_BACKUP_S3_* are exported by the script itself, which is why this profile must never grow a wildcard.

deploy-bench.why: rediacc_ci.ops.deploy_bench pushes the bench Worker's secrets. Bench signs licences with the PRODUCTION ED25519 pair, the same unsuffixed entries the edge and stable profiles bind (operator ruling 2026-10-27), so a released renet verifies bench licences. The X25519 pair, JWT secret and server API key stay DEV: bench configs already hold the DEV X25519 public key as e2ePublicKey. Bench has its own SES and Turnstile credentials, and `rotation check --for=bench` needs the admin set and the three `OBS_READER_SSH_*` reader values, REQUIRED so a store without them refuses before the first remote write. The config server key is `ACCOUNT_CONFIG_SERVER_KEY_BENCH`, the backup pair `ACCOUNT_BACKUP_S3_*_BENCH`, and `BENCH_ROOT_PASSWORD` the root login.

reset-bench.why: rediacc_ci.ops.reset_bench wipes the bench D1 database and the bench config bucket (rediacc-configs-bench). The bucket is listed and emptied over the R2 S3 API, signed with the `CLOUDFLARE_R2_*` trio, and `cf_auth` mints its management token from the global key. Split from deploy-bench (agent/plans/PLAN-backup-credential-isolation.md B2) so that the deploy, which pushes secrets to a public Worker, never holds the R2 trio.

bench-access.why: rediacc_ci.ops.bench_access edits the one WAF custom rule that limits the bench hosts to five IP addresses. `cf_auth.resolve_scoped("bench-access")` mints, from the Global API Key, a token carrying Zone WAF Write on the apex zone only and deletes it at the end of the run; nothing else of the deploy-bench set is needed, which is why this is not that profile.

backup-push-stable.why: rediacc_ci.ops.push_backup_credentials --target stable pushes the four ACCOUNT_BACKUP_S3_* secrets to one of the three stable regional Workers with one `wrangler secret bulk`, outside a release. It binds ONLY the stable key pair (bucket-scoped to rediacc-backups-{eu,us,asia}), renamed to the names the Worker reads, the shared endpoint, and the Workers deploy token; a second environment's pair is refused by check:ci-backup-credential-isolation (agent/plans/PLAN-backup-credential-isolation.md B3).

backup-push-edge.why: rediacc_ci.ops.push_backup_credentials --target edge pushes the four ACCOUNT_BACKUP_S3_* secrets to one of the three edge regional Workers with one `wrangler secret bulk`, outside a release. It binds ONLY the edge key pair (bucket-scoped to edge-rediacc-backups-{eu,us,asia}), renamed to the names the Worker reads, the shared endpoint, and the Workers deploy token; a second environment's pair is refused by check:ci-backup-credential-isolation (agent/plans/PLAN-backup-credential-isolation.md B3).

backup-push-bench.why: rediacc_ci.ops.push_backup_credentials --target bench pushes the four ACCOUNT_BACKUP_S3_* secrets to one of the bench Worker with one `wrangler secret bulk`, outside a release. It binds ONLY the bench key pair (bucket-scoped to rediacc-backups-bench), renamed to the names the Worker reads, the shared endpoint, and the Workers deploy token; a second environment's pair is refused by check:ci-backup-credential-isolation (agent/plans/PLAN-backup-credential-isolation.md B3).

deploy-proxy-bench.why: rediacc_ci.deploy.deploy_proxy --target bench deploys the bench proxy Worker and its executor image (workers/proxy/wrangler.bench.toml), re-executing itself under this profile when it is not bound. wrangler needs the Workers deploy token and the account id; the renet the image ships is built with the licence public key, and bench signs with the production keypair (operator ruling 2026-10-27: Bench signs with production key), so the production public key is bound, as for edge and stable. Nothing else: the config gate refuses the file before this profile is entered, and the Worker mints its executor token over its ISSUER binding, so no token is put.

deploy-proxy.why: A local stable or edge proxy deploy, `bws_env exec --profile deploy-proxy -- python3 -m rediacc_ci.deploy.deploy_proxy --target edge|stable --region R --version V` (CD binds the same names through its own bws step). wrangler needs the Workers deploy token and the account id; the image is built from the release's executor artifacts, which `executor_artifacts fetch` reads from the releases R2 bucket with the R2 trio under the names the aws CLI reads; the production licence public key is the one the artifacts' renet verifies with.

live-console.why: The live console probes (private/account/e2e/playwright.live.config.ts): 27-90 logs in as the ROOT_EMAIL user; 27-91 logs in one member of each of two bench test orgs with password and TOTP, unlocks both stores with one shared store password, runs machine status on LIVE_CONSOLE_MACHINE (hostinger, via the probe key held only in those encrypted configs), and reads the cli.command audit rows of LIVE_CONSOLE_D1_DATABASE through wrangler with the scoped CD token, never the account-wide Global API Key (measured 2026-10-27 through this profile: 7 rows read). LIVE_CONSOLE_PROBE_SSH_KEY is stored for rotation and revocation only and no profile binds it.

live-console-edge-eu.why: The live console probes (private/account/e2e/playwright.live.config.ts, 27-90 and 27-91) against https://edge-eu.rediacc.com: two test orgs of the edge-account-db-eu D1, provisioned by direct D1 writes (PLAN-console-executor-multi-org ML1-ML3), each a PROFESSIONAL member with password and TOTP, one shared store password, and a config holding the hostinger probe key (LIVE_CONSOLE_PROBE_SSH_KEY, bound by no profile). Org A also stands in as the 27-90 member (LIVE_CONSOLE_EMAIL, LIVE_CONSOLE_PASSWORD, LIVE_CONSOLE_TOTP_SECRET). Edge enforces Turnstile on /auth/login, so the probes mint each session through a refresh_tokens row written with the scoped CD token (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) and /auth/refresh; the same token reads the cli.command rows.

live-console-edge-us.why: The live console probes (private/account/e2e/playwright.live.config.ts, 27-90 and 27-91) against https://edge-us.rediacc.com: two test orgs of the edge-account-db-us D1, provisioned by direct D1 writes (PLAN-console-executor-multi-org ML1-ML3), each a PROFESSIONAL member with password and TOTP, one shared store password, and a config holding the hostinger probe key (LIVE_CONSOLE_PROBE_SSH_KEY, bound by no profile). Org A also stands in as the 27-90 member (LIVE_CONSOLE_EMAIL, LIVE_CONSOLE_PASSWORD, LIVE_CONSOLE_TOTP_SECRET). Edge enforces Turnstile on /auth/login, so the probes mint each session through a refresh_tokens row written with the scoped CD token (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) and /auth/refresh; the same token reads the cli.command rows.

live-console-edge-asia.why: The live console probes (private/account/e2e/playwright.live.config.ts, 27-90 and 27-91) against https://edge-asia.rediacc.com: two test orgs of the edge-account-db-asia D1, provisioned by direct D1 writes (PLAN-console-executor-multi-org ML1-ML3), each a PROFESSIONAL member with password and TOTP, one shared store password, and a config holding the hostinger probe key (LIVE_CONSOLE_PROBE_SSH_KEY, bound by no profile). Org A also stands in as the 27-90 member (LIVE_CONSOLE_EMAIL, LIVE_CONSOLE_PASSWORD, LIVE_CONSOLE_TOTP_SECRET). Edge enforces Turnstile on /auth/login, so the probes mint each session through a refresh_tokens row written with the scoped CD token (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) and /auth/refresh; the same token reads the cli.command rows.

bench-login.why: rediacc_ci.ops.login_bench (`npm run login:bench`, operator order 2026-10-27) logs the eu-bench config into https://bench.rediacc.com headless with the operator's own bench account, and refuses every other server and config. The email, password and the six-digit code it derives in memory from the TOTP seed (rediacc_ci.ops.totp) reach `rdc subscription login` only as REDIACC_LOGIN_EMAIL, REDIACC_LOGIN_PASSWORD and REDIACC_LOGIN_TOTP in the child environment; the master password reaches `rdc config remote enable --master-password` only as REDIACC_STORE_MASTER_PASSWORD. Nothing is put on argv or printed. Edge and stable keep human login, so no other environment's account is bound here.

rotation.why: `./run.sh rotation ...` (account_rotation). The admin credentials mint and delete infrastructure; the operator ruled they live in ci-shared (Q2). `passes_token` hands the bootstrap token to the child because the rotation tool writes `bitwarden-sm:` consumers with `bws` itself. `CLOUDFLARE_TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` is optional: `rotation check` probes it through siteverify for the `turnstile` slug (scripts/rotation/commands/check.ts) and falls back to a timestamp heuristic that reports a false drift without it. `rotation check` reads the observability host with the `OBS_READER_SSH_*` trio; optional here because `list|status|history` read no host, and the reader reports an absent value as could-not-check (exit 2).

publish-media.why: The R2 media sync and `--publish-www` upload to the media CDN origin. Without these the run copies locally, uploads nothing and exits 0, which is why .claude/rediacc_hooks/guards/block_host_toolchain_run.py demands the profile in the command.

credential-drift.why: `npm run check:env-credential-drift`, the advisory phase of ./run.sh setup. It compares the IDENTIFIERS local development uses against private/account/rotation-manifest.json. All optional, so a machine with no bootstrap token skips loudly instead of failing setup.

r2-artifacts.why: rediacc_ci.ops.scrub_sentinel and other local R2 artifact-bucket maintenance run by hand. The same three names CI requests for artifact uploads.

config-blob-migration.why: private/account/scripts/migrate-config-blob-keys.ts: the D1 query needs the account id and the scoped Cloudflare token, the R2 S3 calls need the key pair, and the script derives the endpoint from the account id and the bucket's jurisdiction, so `CLOUDFLARE_R2_ENDPOINT` is not bound. One profile instead of nesting deploy-workers and r2-artifacts, which also bound the unneeded Turnstile site key. Since PLAN-backup-credential-isolation B8 (2026-10-20) the `CLOUDFLARE_R2_*` pair is scoped to the releases bucket and rediacc-configs-bench, so this profile reaches the bench config bucket only; every other environment's bucket answers AccessDenied, and all seven environments held 0 rows to move on 2026-10-20.

publish-solutions.why: private/growth/video_pipeline/publish-solutions.sh: uploads the solution videos to R2 (the media keys) and purges the CDN (the Cloudflare global key). It used to `source` the whole account env file for five names.

deploy-workers.why: A local code deploy of the account and www Workers (.claude/skills/deploy): wrangler needs the scoped Cloudflare token and account id, and the portal build needs the Turnstile site key (a keyless portal is a login outage, 2026-09-24). Worker secrets are NOT re-sent by this profile; CI's set_*_worker_secrets steps own them.

telemetry-probe.why: rediacc_ci.ops.telemetry_delivery (PLAN-telemetry-export T16) reads Tempo, Prometheus and Loki through the Grafana datasource proxy at grafana.rediacc.io with the Viewer service account `telemetry-probe` (Grafana id 2); the token is read-only (a datasource write answers 403).

mirror-config-store.why: rediacc_ci.ops.mirror_config_store copies one remote config store from a stable account D1 and config bucket into its edge twin or into bench. `cf_auth.resolve_scoped("mirror-config-store")` mints, from the Global API Key, a token carrying D1 Write, Workers R2 Storage Write and Workers Scripts Read (secret names for the CONFIG_SERVER_KEY presence check) and destroys it at the end of the run. When the store's row is a csk1 row, check_server_key reads the TARGET's key to compare its kid: ACCOUNT_CONFIG_SERVER_KEY_<SUFFIX>_EDGE or ACCOUNT_CONFIG_SERVER_KEY_BENCH, so those are optional names.

cf-usage-report.why: rediacc_ci.ops.cf_usage_report (PLAN-cloudflare-spend-guard T6) reads R2, D1 and Workers usage from the account GraphQL endpoint with the scoped Cloudflare token, and counts the account Worker's 'Nightly maintenance is NOT running' line in Loki through the Grafana datasource proxy with the read-only Viewer token. rediacc_ci.ops.observability_volume (T4) reads the same Grafana token; its telemetry query needs Workers Observability Write, which a local run takes from the Global API Key pair (optional) until the scoped token carries it.

grafana-smtp.why: Grafana alert email on the hostinger observability stack sends through AWS SES EU over SMTP (STARTTLS, port 587). The login is the SES EU access key id, and the password is AWS_SES_SMTP_PASSWORD_EU, the SMTP form derived from the EU secret key, so it must be re-derived and stored again whenever that key rotates. The values reach the stack's secrets.env as GF_SMTP_USER and GF_SMTP_PASSWORD over stdin, never on argv.

account-secrets-eu-stable.why: rediacc_ci.deploy.account_secrets_local --region eu --target stable: the local entry for set_account_worker_secrets on Worker rediacc-account-eu (agent/plans/PLAN-backup-program.md M1). Binds exactly what that script reads for this region and channel: the region's EU-suffixed SES, OTLP, Stripe webhook credentials, the stable backup key pair only, and the Workers deploy token, and the one config server key of this region and channel (ACCOUNT_CONFIG_SERVER_KEY_EU_STABLE, agent/plans/PLAN-config-server-key.md K2), never another environment's; the Turnstile pair is bound for the drift preflight that runs first. Bucket, jurisdiction and SES region are not secrets and come from regions.json.

release-local.why: rediacc_ci.release.local (PLAN-local-release): the release run from the operator's machine. Binds the account public key for the order check, the release GPG pair, the git bot identity, the Cloudflare zone, the R2 artifact trio and the Worker secrets. The edge www Worker reads AWS_SES_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SES_REGION and the STRIPE_* pair, stored as the EU SES pair, AWS_SES_REGION_EU and STRIPE_SANDBOX_*: those are bound here and `_bind` copies them to the read names for that child. `_bind` reads no store and refuses a name no carried profile declares. GHCR and GitHub tokens are written by the session through bws_env store-from-env.
